**Title**: vue-tsc rejects the argument of an imported VaporDirective in SFC
templates after vuejs/core#15490

**Versions**: vue 3.6.0-rc.9; vue-tsc and @vue/language-core as installed
(3.3.11 at the time of writing, the latest release).

**Repro**, two files:

```ts
// directive.ts
import type { VaporDirective } from 'vue';
export const vMark: VaporDirective = (_el, _value, _argument, _modifiers) => {};
```

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup vapor>
import { vMark } from './directive';
</script>
<template>
  <button v-mark:command="'x'">go</button>
</template>
```

`vue-tsc --noEmit`

**Actual**: TS2345, argument of type `string` is not assignable to a parameter of
type `() => unknown` (the ARGUMENT slot).

**Expected**: passes. Since #15490 the compiler emits the argument as a getter
(`() => ("command")`) and the runtime reads it as one, so the .d.ts and the
emitted call agree; the template check is passing the pre-#15490 shape.

**Notes**:

- A directive declared LOCALLY in the SFC with the same signature is not checked
  at all and passes, so the failure is specific to an imported declaration.
- Registering the directive app-wide (`app.directive('mark', vMark)`) also passes,
  but only because there is then no declaration to check - that is opting out of
  checking rather than satisfying it.
- Annotating the import as Vue's own `VaporDirective` does not help.
- core's `dts-test` covers the RUNTIME call shape only; template checking lives in
  this repository, so #15490 appears never to have been checked against it.

### 34.10 H1 in a real production bundle (s35) - VERIFIED, and the model holds

The carried rc.8 item. H1 was V by reading and pinned by
`tests/root-only-prod-fixture.test.ts`, which MODELS a production bundle:
`vi.doMock('vue', throw)`, a fresh registry, `src/` imported directly. This
cycle's own lesson is that a fixture substituting a model for the integration can
only check the half you already understood, so the model was checked against the
thing.

**How it was driven.** Two consumers built with Vite's build API, production,
minified, **Vue BUNDLED** (an app build, not a library one - the page genuinely
has Vapor in it), each entry with its own package.json so `sideEffects` is honoured;
the built chunk then loaded into a happy-dom global the way
`scripts/check-example-directive.mjs` loads the example, a real
`createVaporApp(defineVaporComponent({ setup }))` mounted, and the results read off
a global the entry writes (an app build drops entry exports - the s15 trap). One
arm imports the composables from the ROOT, the control from `vapor-chamber/vue`;
both take the bus from the root. Probe: `.probes/h1-prod-bundle.test.ts`.

    measurement                     root-only        control (/vue)
    __VUE__ seen inside setup()     true             true
    isRef(useCommand().loading)     FALSE            true
    isRef(useCommandState().state)  FALSE            true
    state advances on a dispatch    TRUE             true
    on() listener after unmount     SURVIVES         disposed
    root-only production warning    fires, once      absent

**H1 is confirmed under genuine production conditions**, and the mocked fixture's
model is faithful on every axis it asserts. Two things the real bundle adds:

- **The degradation is "not reactive", not "not updating".** The reducer still
  runs and `state.value` still advances; what is missing is the notification, so a
  template bound to it never re-renders. A test written to assert that the value
  does not change would have been asserting something false. (The first cut of the
  probe read "did not advance" for its own reason: it called
  `bus.register('ping')` and silently replaced `useCommandState`'s own reducer.
  Recorded because the wrong number was believable.)
- **The H1(a) warning fires in a real production bundle**, naming both remedies -
  previously evidence only under the mock. A second warning fires beside it, the
  signal-race heads-up ("3 signals were created before a reactive backing was
  configured"), which is the same defect seen from the other end.

**RECOMMENDATION, now that H1 is V: a documented limitation, with the warning as
the mitigation - not a fix.** The three degradations are one cause, and two of
them cannot be repaired where they happen:

- the signal is plain because `configureSignal` never ran;
- cleanup never arms because `onScopeDispose` is unset;
- the KeepAlive guard is inert because `hasInjectionContext` is unset.

All three need Vue, and the root cannot reach Vue in a production bundle by
construction - a bare `import('vue')` is a specifier the browser cannot resolve.
That is not a bug to fix in `chamber.ts`; it is the reason `vapor-chamber/vue`,
`vapor-chamber/vapor` and `vaporChamberWire()` exist, and all three shipped in
v1.20.0 along with the loud warning. The listener that outlives `app.unmount()`
is the same LEAK SHAPE as rc9/4, but not the same kind of defect: rc9/4 was a
guard of ours returning early and the fix was deleting it, while here there is
nothing to delete - the cleanup call has no `onScopeDispose` to make. The
structural fix is already on the books as the v2 identity decision (13.4 P1,
delete the async probe so this state is loud in DEV too), and nothing smaller
changes the outcome.

So: v1.22.0 states it as a known limitation, in the words the measurement
supports - the value still advances, it is simply not reactive - and the warning
is what stands between a consumer and silence. Owner's call to accept that.

**Not promoted to the suite, deliberately.** The cheap fixture already guards the
behaviour in milliseconds; committing this one would make every run pay two Vite
builds forever to re-assert what it asserts. It is an instrument, not a guard:
its job was to check the model against reality once, and it did. Re-run it when
the model's premises change - a new entry, a change to the probe in chamber.ts, or
a Vue release that alters when `__VUE__` is written.

### 34.11 `a5f7a2c1`: a class binding wipes our state classes, on BOTH renderers

Queue item 3, and it did not stay a pass-through row. rc.9's `a5f7a2c1` is "keep
transition classes when updating class binding". `v-vc:command` writes
`vc-loading` and `vc-error` onto the same classList by hand, so the question was
whether they survive a `:class` update.

**Read at source first** (installed rc.9): runtime-vapor's `setClass()` ends in
`el.className = value` - a wholesale assignment - unless a transition is enabled,
in which case it calls runtime-dom's `patchClass()`, which is

    const transitionClasses = el[vtcKey];
    if (transitionClasses) value = (value ? [value, ...transitionClasses] : [...transitionClasses]).join(' ');
    ... el.className = value;

so `a5f7a2c1` preserves EXACTLY the classes Vue itself recorded in `el[vtcKey]`
and nothing else. A third path, `setClassIncremental()`, runs when `el.$root` is
set (a component root taking a fallthrough class) and uses `classList.add/remove`,
removing only what it previously set.

**Measured** (`.probes/class-binding.test.ts`; compiled templates on the installed
Vue through `tests/compile-vapor.ts`, a real mount, `classList.add('vc-loading')`
standing in for what `buildHandler` does at dispatch, then the bound class changed
and `nextTick` awaited):

    arm                                          className after the :class update
    Vapor, element that is NOT the component root   "b"            vc-loading WIPED
    Vapor, component root (class as fallthrough)    "vc-loading b" survives
    vDOM, element that is NOT the component root    "b"            vc-loading WIPED

**So this is not an rc.9 regression and not Vapor-specific: it is a defect of our
own directive on both renderers, as old as the directive.** An element carrying
both `v-vc:command` and a `:class` binding loses `vc-loading` the moment that
binding updates - the button still works and still dispatches, but the loading
style vanishes mid-flight, and `vc-error` can be wiped immediately after being
set. It survives only by the accident of the element being a component root.

**One correction recorded, because the first number was believable.** The first cut
of the probe used a single-root `<button :class="cls">` template, which makes the
button the component ROOT - so both arms took `setClassIncremental` and both
reported "survives". One path measured twice, reported as two. The nested template
is what separates them.

**IT IS NOT A CLASS PROBLEM. `disabled` goes the same way, and that half is not
cosmetic.** The directive also writes `el.disabled = true` at dispatch start
(`src/directives.ts:280`) and `false` at settle (327). Measured in the same probe,
Vapor, non-root element with `:disabled="d"`:

    set by hand                          -> true
    after a SAME-VALUE binding update    -> true    (Vue does not re-assert)
    after the binding CHANGES value      -> FALSE   (wiped)

The same-value row is the mechanism stated exactly: Vue compares against the
previous BINDING value, not against the live DOM property (rc.6 #15343 moved that
comparison onto a `$p$` expando), so a hand-written value survives until the
binding next moves and is then overwritten wholesale.

**CORRECTION, and it is the cost of a grep.** The paragraph that stood here said
the wipe defeats the re-entry guard and lets a second click dispatch. It does not.
`buildHandler` checks `if (state.loading) return;` FIRST (`src/directives.ts:266`)
and only then `el.disabled === true` (267). `state.loading` is internal, a binding
cannot touch it, so re-entrancy stays blocked whatever happens to the DOM property.
The claim came from reading 267 and 280 out of a grep and missing the line two
above; it was published in rc9/25 and is retracted here rather than quietly edited.

What the wipe actually costs, stated to the measurement: mid-dispatch the button
stops LOOKING disabled and accepts clicks that then do nothing. That is an
inconsistency a user can see, not a double dispatch. The `disabled` half is
therefore no more severe than the class half - both are presentation - and the
finding's weight rests on the shape, not on a correctness escalation that turned
out not to exist.

The finding is therefore **"a bound update overwrites state the directive wrote by
hand"**, of which the class case is one instance. A `data-vc-state` channel
addresses the class half only - `disabled` has to be a real DOM property, because
the platform and the guard both read it.

**Flagged, not chased** (queue rule). It touches a documented CSS contract -
`.vc-loading` and `.vc-error` are in the README, the whitepaper 10.3 and
`examples/feature-directives.html` - so it is an owner DECISION, not a fix to slip
in. The options, with what each costs:

  a. **Document the collision**: do not put `:class` on the same element. Cheapest,
     and it leaves a silent failure in place for anyone who does.
  b. **A second channel**: also write `data-vc-state="loading" | "error"`, which
     `setClass` never touches, and document CSS against the attribute. Additive,
     a few bytes, keeps the classes for compatibility; two sources of truth until
     the classes are retired.
  c. **Re-assert after the binding writes.** THIS OPTION WAS WRITTEN WRONG THE
     FIRST TIME: it said "no hook exists to do it from", which is true of Vapor
     and false of vDOM, where the directive has an `updated` hook. Measured: on a
     `:class` update the hook runs AFTER the patch (it sees `"b"`, with
     `vc-loading` already gone) and re-adding there holds - final className
     `"b vc-loading"`. So vDOM can keep the documented `.vc-loading` contract with
     no API change at all. Vapor still cannot: it has no `updated` by design
     (rc9/3), and opening a `renderEffect` is the import D3 declined on Vue 3.5
     link-time grounds.
  d. **Write into `el[vtcKey]`**: Vue-internal, shared with transitions, and it
     would make our classes look like transition classes to Vue. No.

**The answer is therefore split, which no single option above states:**

  - **vDOM**: re-assert in `updated` (option c). Measured to work, no API change,
    covers both the class and the `disabled` half.
  - **Vapor**: no hook, so either `data-vc-state` for the classes plus an accepted
    limit on `disabled`, or a declared limitation for both.

**Found by reading the file end to end, and unrelated to rc.9**: the header of
`src/directives.ts` documents three CSS classes (line 238), and `vc-success`
- "briefly added on success (removed after 1 tick)" - appears nowhere else in
`src`, in the tests, in the docs or in the examples. It is documented behaviour
the code does not have, in the same list as the two classes that are real. Either
add it or delete the line; it is one line either way, and it is not this cycle's.

Recommendation: take the split - (c) on vDOM, and a declared limitation on Vapor
for this release - and make the Vapor half its own item with its own decision row,
sized first. Not taken here: this is a pre-existing, both-renderer defect, and the
v1.22.0 claim is an RC alignment. Widening it now is how the last cycle's scope
grew. v1.22.0 states it as a known limitation instead, with the root-versus-non-root
detail, since that detail is what decides whether a given consumer sees it.

### 34.12 The Vue-touching src map (s36, 2026-09-21)

Ordered by how a file reaches Vue, because that is what decides its failure mode.
Every file below was re-opened in full for this map; a read from before the
context break was treated as TV and redone. Line numbers are from those reads.

The comments quoted here are the "enables" candidates: each one records a
decision that depends on Vue behaving a particular way, so each is a place an
RC can change the answer.

#### A. Static `import ... from 'vue'` - a rename is a consumer BUILD error

**`src/vue.ts` (132)** - `ref`, `shallowRef`, `getCurrentScope`,
`getCurrentInstance`, `hasInjectionContext`, `onScopeDispose`, `onActivated`,
`onDeactivated` from `vue`; `pauseTracking` / `resetTracking` from
`@vue/reactivity`.
- "THE LIST IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATIVE" (37-59): `hasInjectionContext` was
  missing until v1.17.0, which silently disabled the KeepAlive guard in a
  production bundle only. Any new registry entry `chamber.ts` reads must be
  added here or it exists for probe-path consumers alone.
- "@vue/reactivity and not vue" (93-98): re-verified by enumerating BOTH modules
  at 3.6.0-rc.6 - the four tracking primitives are undefined on `vue`. An
  RC that moved them onto `vue` would be an "enables" (one fewer peer).
- SCOPE (31-35): named imports only; `import * as Vue` measured at 3x bundle
  size on the vapor-sfc example. Vapor names are excluded because importing a
  missing name is a LINK error on 3.5, not a soft failure.

**`src/vapor.ts` (148)** - `createVaporApp`, `defineVaporComponent`,
`defineVaporAsyncComponent`. Re-exports `./vue`, which is what evaluates it.
- WIRED SET (86-122): a five-row measured table of what each additional wired
  name costs the vapor-sfc bundle. `defineVaporCustomElement` (+9.21 KB raw)
  and `vaporInteropPlugin` (+78.27 KB, ~2x the app) are deliberately NOT wired;
  a consumer wires them by hand because `configureVue` merges. Any rc.9 change
  to what those two drag in moves this table.
- Relies on `configureVue` MERGING and on every assignment in `applyVueModule`
  being `typeof`-guarded, so evaluation order between `./vue` and this file
  cannot matter.

**`src/store.ts` (258)** - `shallowRef`, `getCurrentScope`, `onScopeDispose`,
type `ShallowRef`.
- "VUE IS IMPORTED STATICALLY, not resolved through chamber.ts's registry"
  (34-41): the probe is behind both shipped prod-only bugs; a static import
  turns an upstream rename into a build error rather than a runtime null.
- "SHALLOW, REPLACED WHOLESALE" (53-59): ~3.4x over a deep `ref` on array state
  (tests/signal-shallow-ab.test.ts). A reducer that mutates and returns the
  same object is a no-op to the signal - that is a Vue-semantics dependency.
- `getCurrentScope()` gates the holder count; the LAST holder out disposes
  (106-124), after a measured bug where the FIRST scope's unmount killed a
  store two components still held.

**`src/router/index.ts` (592)** - `computed`, `getCurrentScope`,
`onScopeDispose`, `shallowRef`.
- `install()` (563-572) deliberately does NOT `app.component('RouterOutlet')`:
  a global registration is a live reference from the router to a vDOM
  component, which pins Vue's virtual-DOM runtime into every consumer's bundle,
  Vapor apps included. vue-router hit the same wall.
- `resolveRender` imports `./blade` on demand (301-306) for the same reason -
  one extra chunk the first time a blade row is hit, versus the vDOM runtime in
  every Vapor graph.
- `scoped()` (512-516) auto-disposes guards/hooks through `getCurrentScope`,
  no-op outside a scope: the house contract for every composable here.

**`src/router/engine.ts` (588)** - `shallowRef` only.
- Header (1-3): "Vue 3.6-native: router state IS a shallowRef
  (alien-signals-backed in 3.6) - no bridge layer." The whole module's design
  rests on 3.6 reactivity being cheap enough to hold a frozen snapshot per
  commit.
- `START_LOCATION` (42-71) is frozen UNCONDITIONALLY rather than under DEV like
  `../freeze`, because it is a module-level singleton shared by every router in
  the process - four empty objects frozen once, no per-commit cost to weigh.

**`src/router/composables.ts` (314)** - `Ref`, `computed`, `customRef`,
`getCurrentScope`, `inject`, `onScopeDispose`.
- `QueryParamHandle` (29-46) and `useQueryParam` (66-82): `customRef`, NOT a
  hand-rolled `{ get value() }`. The reason is a Vue behaviour - refs returned
  from `setup()` are AUTO-UNWRAPPED in templates and a lookalike object is not,
  which made this the one composable whose templates needed `.value`.
  Dependency tracking still flows through `router.currentRoute` read inside
  `get()`; `track()`/`trigger()` are not the source of truth, the URL is.

**`src/router/outlet.ts` (32)** - `defineComponent`, `h`, `inject`, `provide`.
- Keyless on purpose (6-8): the same record at a depth keeps its instance
  across param/query changes, a different record swaps it. That is Vue's own
  identity rule used as the reuse-vs-remount contract.

**`src/router/blade.ts` (52)** - `defineComponent`, `h`, `onMounted`,
`onBeforeUnmount`, `shallowRef`.
- The two `!el.value` guards (29-36) are TYPE narrowing, unreachable through
  this component's own lifecycle, and the reason given is Vue's ordering: Vue
  binds template refs before `onMounted` and nulls them only after
  `onBeforeUnmount`. Measured 4/4 false, 0 true - so `v8 ignore`, not a test.
- `shallowRef` because the value is a DOM element, "which has no business being
  reactive at all"; `ref()` would leave it unproxied anyway, but relying on
  that is called an accident rather than a rule.

**`src/router/vapor.ts` (134)** - `createDynamicComponent`, `createSlot`,
`defineVaporComponent`, `inject`, `provide`.
- The densest "until Vue does X" file in the tree. The mode guard (70-102) exists
  because upstream has NONE to inherit: `createDynamicComponent` gates its vnode
  branch on `appContext.vdom`, so with no interop a vDOM component does not
  error, it falls through to Vapor-mode creation - wrong-mode rendering with no
  upstream diagnostic. The guard reads `__vapor === true`, which
  `defineVaporComponent` stamps.
- `createSlot` is built ONCE in setup, never inside the branch getter (116-127):
  it reads the current scope owner and allocates a fragment per call, so one
  call per navigation would leak fragments and defeat branch keying. The
  no-slot case must reach `createDynamicComponent` as a LITERAL null.
- "The helpers used here are what compiled Vapor SFCs call, not documented
  user-facing API" (51-54) - `tests/vapor/vapor-outlet-helpers.test.ts`
  enumerates that surface so an upstream rename fails here first. `slots` is
  named as the ninth item: Vapor's `setup` receives the component INSTANCE as
  its second argument and there is no public slot-existence helper.
- Size note (56-60): held to 0.5 KB brotli, the whole DEV branch is one inline
  dead expression so a consumer's prod build drops both message variants in one
  step.

**`src/router/revalidate.ts` (222)** - `shallowRef` only, for its own
`isRevalidating`.
- "WHY THE PLUGIN OWNS ITS `isRevalidating`" (33-38): `router.isRevalidating` is
  `Readonly` and its only writer is the engine's `trackRevalidation`. Driving it
  would mean casting the readonly away and becoming a second writer to another
  module's state. Two sources, two flags; a consumer ORs them.

**`src/router/router-type.ts` (69)** - type `ShallowRef` only. Exists so
`outlet.ts` and `composables.ts` type against the Router without importing the
implementation. `install` is typed to take only `{ provide }` (63-67) so the
type cannot contradict the implementation's deliberate non-registration.

**`src/router/vdom.ts` (22)** - no `vue` import of its own; a re-export barrel
for `outlet` + `blade`. "The subpath is named for what it costs" (11-13).

#### B. Runtime lookup - dev-correct, prod-degraded by construction

**`src/chamber.ts` (1646)** - reaches Vue ONLY through `import('vue')` and
`import('@vue/reactivity')`, both with the specifier held in a variable, plus
two global slots. Registry entries read: `shallowRef`/`ref`, `onScopeDispose`,
`getCurrentScope`, `getCurrentInstance`, `hasInjectionContext`, `onActivated`,
`onDeactivated`, `createVaporApp`, `vaporInteropPlugin`,
`defineVaporCustomElement`, `defineVaporComponent`, `defineVaporAsyncComponent`.
- `VUE_GLOBAL_KEY` (194-206): distinct from `__VUE__` on purpose, because Vue
  assigns the BOOLEAN `true` to `__VUE__` from `prepareApp()` (Vapor) and
  `baseCreateRenderer()` (vDOM) - so a namespace parked there dies the moment
  anything mounts. A pure Vue-behaviour dependency, pinned by a test.
- `tryKeepAliveHooks` (753-796): must NOT be `getCurrentInstance()`, which reads
  vDOM's `currentInstance` and returns null inside `defineVaporComponent`.
  Marked PERMANENT on the rc.5 cycle: vuejs/core#13687, a core maintainer
  confirmed the null is intentional and Vapor exposes no component instance
  tree to userland by design. "Do not restore an instance-accessor probe here
  on the theory that it will start working."
- `tryAutoCleanup` (685-721): records rc.6's per-render HMR scope (9ab65a1) and
  rc.8's never-mounted-component disposal (efa2eae) as cases where "the cleanup
  was always on the right scope, and Vue began stopping it". Both are the
  shape an rc.9 "enables" would take.
- `applyVueModule` (115-142): `shallowRef` over `ref` on the dispatch path,
  with the number corrected in place - ~1.2x scalar reproduces, ~1.5x never
  appeared once. Also states the inversion: outside the dispatch path
  `ref(primitive)` never builds a proxy and the two swap.
- `probeVue` (485-525): "Do NOT try to fix a miss here with a second dynamic
  import of the with-vapor build" - two separately-imported Vue dist files are
  two disconnected reactivity engines, verified, silent.
- `warnProbePath` / `warnUnwired` (345-430): the H1 diagnostics. The second is
  deliberately NOT dev-gated, because the state it reports exists only in
  production.

**`src/vite-hmr.ts` (666)** - runs in Vite's Node process and is never bundled
into an app; it EMITS `import * as __VC_VUE__ from 'vue'` into a virtual module
(247-254) and duplicates `VUE_GLOBAL_KEY` rather than importing it, so the
plugin does not pull the detection module's load-time probe into a build tool.
- v1.19.0 (20-35): the transform claimed `.vue` and had never delivered a shim
  to one - `enforce: 'pre'` puts it ahead of @vitejs/plugin-vue, so it
  prepended to RAW SFC text, which compiler-sfc discards without a diagnostic.
  Proven by byte-identical `transformRequest` output.
- v1.17.0 (36-58): rc.6's per-render EffectScope and the `isHmrUpdating` reset,
  both recorded as changing what a hot reload does to a preserved bus.
- `vaporChamberWire` (400-498): the H1 build-time remedy; build-only on a
  measurement (the dev-server redirect put two chamber modules in the page).

#### C. Vue-dependent without importing Vue - the registry consumers

**`src/chamber-vapor.ts` (325)** - no `vue` import at all; every Vapor API comes
through `chamber.ts`'s getters, which is why each wrapper has a documented
`null` path.
- `devWarnNoVapor` (39-60): the null stays (throwing would break the contract
  and its tests) but is no longer quiet, because "silent negatives are how
  detection bugs survive" - naming the rc.4 KeepAlive bug.
- `useVaporAsyncCommand` (272-279) records the rc.8 finding: an awaiting
  `<script setup vapor>` compiles to an `async setup()` using
  `withAsyncContext`, registers with the NEAREST `<Suspense>`, and composables
  called after the `await` arm cleanup on the restored scope.
- Its dispatch wrapper is hand-rolled, NOT `runDispatch` (291-295): ~1.2x
  leaner than the `.then`-chain, measured. `untracked` wraps the SYNCHRONOUS
  entry only.

**`src/directives.ts` (616)** - no `vue` import; the vDOM half is an
`app.directive()` options object and the Vapor half is the plain function shape
`withVaporDirectives` calls. This is the file rc.9 actually broke.
- Header rc.9 row (6-17) and `vcCommandVapor` (452-489): the argument is a
  getter and ONLY a getter, because Vue's `VaporDirective` declares
  `argument?: () => Arg` with no union. Accepting the string would mean a branch
  no installable Vue can reach.
- "WHY UPSTREAM MADE IT A GETTER, which is not in the commit message" (464-469):
  so DYNAMIC arguments are reactive - Vue's own test reads `arg()` inside a
  `watchEffect`. Here the argument is a SELECTOR, read once at registration.
- The latch (470-489) holds in BOTH directions and on BOTH renderers, measured.
- `beforeUnmount` (565-578) has NO `binding.arg` guard, unlike `mounted` and
  `updated`: teardown is keyed to what was MOUNTED, never to the current
  binding. The guard that used to stand there left a listener dispatching past
  `app.unmount()` for the life of the page.
- `.delegate` (113-157) mirrors rc.2's #15127 opt-in, and is MEASURED as ~1.3x
  SLOWER on mount+unmount - the payoff is standing listener count, not speed.
- `buildHandler` (260-268) mirrors beta.15's "skip disabled delegated direct
  handlers" for the direct listener this directive attaches, and checks
  `state.loading` BEFORE `el.disabled` - internal state a binding cannot reach.

**`src/signal.ts` (97)** - no `vue` import. Reads `globalThis.__VUE__`
synchronously (32-47), preferring `shallowRef` over `ref` for the same
wholesale-replacement reason. "Standalone module with NO module-load side
effects" so transports/plugins/form can import it without dragging the
detection registry into ESM consumer bundles.
- `_plainCreations` / `_raceWarned` (49-95): signals created before a reactive
  backing arrives stay plain FOREVER. That race is exactly H1's mechanism seen
  from the signal side.

**`src/reactive.ts` (84)** - no `vue` import; `deepSignal` calls
`getVueDeepRefFn()` and falls back to the shallow `signal()` when Vue is not yet
detected. The whole subpath exists because the core wires `shallowRef`, and it
says why (1-19): ~3.4x on the `useCommandState` array path.

**`src/transitions.ts` (411)** - no `vue` import; the nine hooks are a shape Vue
calls. Dense with per-release Vue behaviour:
- Header (6-21): rc.8's declared `on*` prop merge made `<Transition v-bind="t"
  @enter="mine">` run both hooks - rc.7 kept only the later source and dropped
  the bridge's `onEnter`. beta.16 inherited onLeave correctness; beta.15
  restored move hooks after a skipped move; beta.14 suppressed `onMove` for
  v-show-hidden children.
- `assembleBridge` (284-315): the nine hooks are ENUMERABLE and `phase` /
  `dispose` are not, because `v-bind="obj"` spreads own enumerable keys and Vue
  passes unmatched ones through as fallthrough ATTRIBUTES - measured rendering
  `phase="[object Object]" dispose="() => {}"` into the DOM since v1.1.0.
- `dispatchWithDone` (192-210): Vue waits for `done()` INDEFINITELY, so a
  handler that never settles left the element stuck for the life of the page.
- `prefixed` (128-148) retires an explicit "DO NOT consolidate, costs ~1%" note
  by removing the hot path rather than paying the 1%.

**`src/ssr.ts` (311)** - no `vue` import at all. Its Vue dependency is purely
POSITIONAL: `rehydrate()`'s command replay sits ABOVE Vue's DOM hydration, so
four releases of hydration fixes (rc.2's #15131/#15132/#15147/#15145,
beta.17's #14972, beta.16's seven, beta.15, beta.13's five) are recorded as
pass-through with the reason stated each time - "they only hand replay a
more-correct DOM". This file is the cleanest example in the tree of a
documented NON-dependency, and it is worth keeping that way.

**`src/alien-signals.ts` (95)** - the deliberate absence. No Vue, and the
connector takes alien-signals' `signal` as an ARGUMENT rather than importing it.
Records that Vue 3.6's `ref()` is itself a port of alien-signals
(vuejs/core#12349), so a Vue consumer is already on it; this exists for
non-Vue consumers. `AlienSignalWrapper` is a class "so V8 gets a stable hidden
class across all adapter instances".

**`src/devtools.ts` (197)** - imports `@vue/devtools-api` only, never `vue`, and
through a variable specifier. The boundary note (96-111) is a Vue-ecosystem
constraint rather than a Vue-runtime one: from the barrel that specifier would
land in every consumer's pre-bundle and their dev server dies at resolve. It
must NEVER be re-exported from `src/index.ts`.

#### What this map changes for the table

Twelve files reach Vue statically and eleven of those are the router; the whole
non-router Vue surface is `vue.ts`, `vapor.ts` and `store.ts`. Everything else
depends on Vue through a registry, a global, or a function SHAPE - which is why
an upstream signature change (rc.9's #15490) surfaces as a dead control rather
than as a build error, and why the shape-dependent files
(`directives.ts`, `transitions.ts`, `chamber-vapor.ts`, `router/vapor.ts`) are
where the 73 TV commits are most likely to bite.

### 34.13 The notice rows re-checked against the map, and the first enables check (s36)

The map (s34.12) was built before the table was re-read, and it immediately

#### `0e4ff650` - the premise was false, the conclusion happens to hold

It was marked `notice` with the reason "reaches consumers only through an API we
re-export". The map falsifies that in one line: `src/router/vapor.ts` is a
group A file and calls `createDynamicComponent` itself, with a mode guard it
carries precisely because upstream has none.

Re-read at source. The commit changes `resolveValue` in
`packages/runtime-vapor/src/apiCreateDynamicComponent.ts` from

    if (type !== 'string' && type !== 'object' && type !== 'function' && type !== 'symbol')

to

    if (!resolved || (type !== 'string' && ... && type !== 'symbol'))

so a FALSY non-null resolved value now takes the empty-branch path instead of
being rendered as a tag. The headline case is `''`.

Traced against what our outlet can actually produce. Its getter returns one of
three things, and none of them is a falsy non-null value:

  - a Vapor component object - `vaporComponentOf` returns it only on
    `__vapor === true` and throws `mode_mismatch` otherwise;
  - `createSlot('default')`, a fragment - `isBlock` returns it untouched
    before `resolveValue` is reached at all;
  - a LITERAL `null`, which the module's own comment says "is what renders a
    true empty branch".

The null path, read end to end at rc.9 and rc.8:

    isBlock(null)                -> false   (all four predicates null-safe:
                                             instanceof Node, isArray,
                                             isVaporComponent -> instanceof,
                                             isFragment -> !!(val && val.__vf))
    resolveDynamicComponent(null)-> NULL_DYNAMIC_COMPONENT   (Symbol.for('v-ndc'))
    rc.8 guard                   -> typeof 'symbol' passes, returns the symbol
    rc.9 guard                   -> !resolved is FALSE (a symbol is truthy),
                                    symbol arm passes, returns the symbol
    caller                       -> resolved === NULL_DYNAMIC_COMPONENT
                                    -> frag.update(undefined, resolved)
                                    -> empty branch

Identical on both releases. So: **direct contact in a group A file, no
behaviour change for this library.**

The status word. The owner asked for "breaks" or "enables"; the measurement
supports neither, and forcing it into one would be the third time this cycle a

**Check 2 - grep the scripts' inserted strings for a `$` sequence.** The first
attempt at this returned CLEAN on `amend-34.mjs` - the script that caused the
corruption - and that false all-clear is worth more than the check itself.

The reason: in the SOURCE the hazard is written `\`$p$\`` inside a template
literal, i.e. dollar followed by a BACKSLASH. The dollar-backtick pair only

meaning to against a string pattern - `$$`, `$&`, dollar-backtick,
dollar-quote. (`$1`-`$9` need capture groups, which a string pattern has none
of, so those stay literal.) It was validated against the known positive before
being trusted:

#### `54097087` read at source - CLAIMED AS ENABLES, RETRACTED IN s34.16

    changed: one word, in compiler-sfc's top-level-await walker.
             `exit(node)` -> `leave(node)`. The walker is estree-walker, whose
             hook is `leave`, so the handler had NEVER RUN and the
             `scope.pop()` inside it was dead code. The scope stack only grew.
    breaks : nothing of ours. It repairs codegen that was already wrong.
    enables: YES, and it is consumer-facing rather than a change we can make.

The walker decides whether a top-level `await` needs separating, by asking
whether it is in the root scope or "not the first statement in a nested block
scope". With the pop dead, the stack was wrong after leaving any nested block,
so a later `await` was misclassified and the emitted `setup()` threw at
runtime. Upstream's added test is exactly that shape:

    if (true) {
      if (false) {}
      await Promise.resolve(1)
      await Promise.resolve(2)
    }

WHY IT IS OURS. `useVaporAsyncCommand`'s contract is stated against this
machinery, and `tests/async-vapor-setup-fixture.test.ts` does not model the
compiler - it CALLS it: `compileScript(descriptor, { id: 'vc-async-setup',
inlineTemplate: true })` from the installed `vue/compiler-sfc`, the very
function this commit fixes. Its SFC awaits at the TOP level
(`await state.gate;`), so it exercises the path but not the shape the bug
broke.

So rc.9 widens the set of consumer source shapes over which our documented
condition holds: a `<script setup vapor>` that awaits inside a nested block -
`if (ready) { await dispatch('a'); await dispatch('b') }`, an ordinary thing to
write - compiled to throwing output on rc.8 and compiles correctly on rc.9.

Evidence for the deliverable list: the one-word diff above; the fixture's own
call into `compileScript`; upstream's #15465 test.

FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE, not taken here (the queue rule, and the owner's
"finish the batch first"): one added case in
`tests/async-vapor-setup-fixture.test.ts` with the await inside a nested block
would pin the widened contract. One SFC string, no new file, no new harness.

**First, the definition.** "Enables" means something that lets this library
delete, simplify or speed up code in `src/`, with the src line cited. Nothing
in `src` changes because of an upstream compiler fix, so even the best version
of this finding does not qualify. The gate set for it was: does a doc or JSDoc
caveat exist that the fix makes obsolete - a note telling consumers to keep
awaits at the top level, or to avoid awaiting inside blocks?

**Checked, and no such caveat exists.** `useVaporAsyncCommand`'s JSDoc
(`chamber-vapor.ts:258-285`), the generated `docs/api/vapor.md` and
`docs/api/index.md` entries derived from it, `ROADMAP.md`'s VaporSuspense row
and the whitepaper's rc.8 row were all read. The whitepaper's rc.8 row says
"commits 11/20 - `useCommand()` after a top-level await arms its cleanup ...
that already held on rc.7", which is a statement of fact, not a caveat to
retire. Nothing anywhere restricts where a consumer may place an `await`.

So by the definition: **not an enables. 0 for the cycle.**

**Second, and worse: the behavioural claim was never measured.** s34.15 stated
that a nested-block await "compiled to throwing output on rc.8 and compiles
correctly on rc.9". That was inferred from the commit message and upstream's
test, not measured, and it does not survive measurement.

Measured properly. rc.8's `@vue/compiler-sfc` was fetched into the scratchpad
and both compilers were run over the same SFC. They differ by ONE CHARACTER -
rc.9 emits `;(` where rc.8 emits `(`:

     11 | if (true) {
     12 |   if (false) {}
     13 |   ;(                      <- rc.9; rc.8 has `(`
     14 |   ([__temp,__restore] = _withAsyncContext(() => Promise.resolve(1))),
     15 |   await __temp,
     16 |   __restore()
     17 | );

A BlockStatement cannot absorb a following `(` as a call, so rc.8's output is
valid JavaScript and its `setup()` RESOLVES. The missing `;` is defensive and
only bites when the preceding statement is an expression that could swallow the
parenthesis.

Six await shapes were tried - top level, upstream's own #15465 repro, after a
sibling block, inside a `for`, inside a `switch` case, and a nested block
followed by top-level awaits. The emitted text differs in three of the six, and
in ALL SIX both compilers produce working output. **No shape was found where
rc.8 throws and rc.9 does not.**

Two harness faults were hit and fixed on the way, both of which would have
produced a confident wrong answer:

- the first import-stripper did not handle `a as b` aliases, so BOTH arms threw
  the same `SyntaxError` - my bug, presented as if it were the compiler's;
- `inlineTemplate: true` emits a `_template(...)` call the harness did not
  stub, so both arms threw `_template is not a function` and the comparison
  concluded nothing. Compiling without `inlineTemplate` isolates the setup body,
  which is the half under test.

The finding that SURVIVES is small and worth one line in the upgrade notes:
rc.9 emits a defensive semicolon before an await sequence that rc.8 omitted,
in await shapes that follow a nested block. No consumer-visible difference was
found for it.

#### What was added anyway, and labelled as what it is

One case in `tests/async-vapor-setup-fixture.test.ts`: the documented contract
with the awaits inside a nested block. It passes on rc.9 and, by the
measurement above, would pass on rc.8 - so it is **coverage, not a
fails-before**, and the note at the end of that file says so in those words,
including the one-character diff and the six shapes.

It still earns its place: the fixture CALLS the real `compileScript`, its
original SFC awaits only at the top level, and awaiting inside a block is an
ordinary thing for a consumer to write. 4 tests pass, `tsc` clean.

#### CORRECTION 1: `80b3a046` DOES break us, and the row answers a different question

The landed row reads: "no, and we do not depend on the order either way -
buildHandler reads `dataset.vcPayload` and `el.disabled` at DISPATCH time, not at
mount."

That is true, and it settles the ordering of the directive against the ELEMENT'S
OWN PROPS. It does not settle the other ordering the same commit moves: our
`addEventListener` against a template's own `@click` `addEventListener` on the
same element. What changed at mount is not what we READ - it is WHEN WE REGISTER.

MEASURED, both compilers, one template
(`<div><button v-vc:command="'cartAdd'" @click="mine">go</button></div>`;
compiler-vapor installed at each version in turn under the scratchpad, the repo's
package.json and lock untouched):

    rc.8   _withVaporDirectives(n0, [[_directive_vc, () => ('cartAdd'), "command"]])
           _on(n0, "click", e => _ctx.mine(e))

    rc.9   _on(n0, "click", e => _ctx.mine(e))
           _withVaporDirectives(n0, [[_directive_vc, () => ('cartAdd'), () => ("command")]])

Our listener was first and is now second. (The rc.8 line also carries the argument
as the bare string `"command"`, which corroborates #15490 from a second direction.)
On the rc.9 runtime the template handler observably runs first: it sees
`vc-loading=false`, the class our synchronous prologue adds.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS A DEAD BUTTON, not a reordering. `buildHandler` bails on
`state.loading`, then on `el.disabled === true` (src/directives.ts:266-268).
Running second puts that guard within a template handler's reach for the first
time. MEASURED on compiled templates: a template `@click` that does the ordinary
`e.currentTarget.disabled = true`, or `e.stopImmediatePropagation()`, suppresses
the dispatch entirely - `[]` where rc.8's order gives `['cartAdd']`. No error, no
warning, no class.

The order alone is the cause, isolated rather than inferred: rc.8's runtime is not
installed, and rc.8's compiler emits the string argument that rc.9's
`vcCommandVapor` rejects by design, so compiling with it would confound the two
changes. Instead both registration orders were run on the rc.9 runtime with the
same directive function and the same template handler, only the order swapped:
directive-first dispatches `['cartAdd']`, template-first dispatches `[]`. That arm
shows listener-order semantics against our guards; the compiler A/B above shows
the order moved. The two together are the claim.

SCOPE, HONESTLY: no documented combination regresses.
`examples/feature-directives.html` says in as many words "There is no click handler
anywhere in this file", and documents the directive as owning the whole interaction,
disable-while-busy included. Nothing in the README, the whitepaper or the examples
puts `@click` on a `v-vc:command` element. Nothing forbids it either, and a consumer
who writes it gets silence. This is the shape s34.1 exists for: not a test failing,
a control quietly doing nothing.

OPTIONS, with what each costs:

  a. Document the collision beside the `.delegate` limitation. 0 B, no behaviour
     change, and it leaves the silence in place for anyone who does not read it.
  b. Register in the CAPTURE phase so we run first whatever the emission order.
     It makes `.capture` the default instead of an opt-in and changes `.stop`
     semantics against ancestors - documented behaviour, so a DECISION, not a fix.
  c. Accept it. A handler that disables the element arguably SHOULD suppress the
     dispatch, and our guard is correct in isolation.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), with (c) as the reason it is only documentation. Byte cost 0.
Test cost one case in `tests/directives-vapor-fixture.test.ts` pinning that a
template `@click` runs first on rc.9 - COVERAGE, not a fails-before, since rc.8's
runtime is not installed to fail against. NOT TAKEN HERE: the queue rule, and the
owner's "finish the batch first".

#### CORRECTION 2: `bb5a18f0`'s verdict stands, its reason is falsified

The landed row reads: "Our Vapor export IS a function. The vDOM object registration
reaches Vue only through `app.directive` on the vDOM renderer, never through a Vapor
template."

The second sentence is false, and it takes one line of consumer code to falsify:
`createVaporApp(App).use(createDirectivePlugin())`. The plugin calls
`app.directive('vc', { mounted, updated, beforeUnmount })` on whatever app it is
handed, and a compiled Vapor template's `resolveDirective("vc")` then finds the
OBJECT and hands it to `withVaporDirectives`. That is exactly the path `bb5a18f0`
adds its warning for.

MEASURED, compiled Vapor template on a Vapor app with the plugin installed:

    rc.9   "[Vue warn]: Received a VDOM object directive (hooks: mounted, updated,
            beforeUnmount) in a Vapor template. Vapor directives must be a
            function: (el, value, arg, modifiers) => cleanup."
           app mounts, button renders, control inert, nothing dispatched
    rc.8   the pre-image line in `fa4cbd68` is the bare
           `const ret = dir(element, value, argument, modifiers)`, so the object is
           CALLED: a TypeError at mount, unwrapped (callWithErrorHandling arrives
           with fa4cbd68, after this commit in the chain)

So the verdict is unchanged and if anything stronger: not a break, an upstream
improvement we inherit, turning a hard mount crash into a named DEV warning. What
was wrong was the reason - the path was called unreachable and it is one line away.
This matters here for the same reason s34.13 gave when `0e4ff650`'s premise turned
out false: a row closed on a reason that does not hold is closed by luck.

It also corroborates a v1.20.0 decision rather than reopening it (decisions.md D3):
our install-time "not ported to Vapor" warning was removed when the port landed, and
Vue now covers the case by name.

#### One harness fault, recorded because the wrong number was believable

The first cut of the slot-outlet arm wrote `<components.Child v-vc:command>`, copying
upstream's own spec files. Their `compile` helper passes bindingMetadata that makes
`components.Child` a setup binding; `tests/compile-vapor.ts` passes none, so it
resolved to a NATIVE CUSTOM ELEMENT. The arm reported the directive applying and
dispatching - the exact opposite of the right answer - and the only thing that
caught it was printing `host.innerHTML` beside the result, where it read
`<components.child>`. Registering the child with `app.component('Child', Child)` is
the fix. Print the DOM next to every claim about the DOM.

Owner ruling on the break s34.19 found: the three guards in `buildHandler`

beta.15 row, both read at source this window), mirroring Vue #14948 for the
DIRECT listener this directive attaches. On rc.9 a template `@click` registers
first and can veto the dispatch; that is the contract working, and what changed
is who runs first. Documented, not fixed. Landed as `rc9/38`, gate green on the
committed tree, 11 steps.

Four places: both JSDoc sites in `src/directives.ts` (+61 lines, ZERO lines of
code), the v1.22.0 CHANGELOG upgrade note with the per-veto table, one compiled
three-arm case in `tests/directives-vapor-fixture.test.ts` labelled COVERAGE at
the top and argued at the end of the file, and a dated `docs/decisions.md` row.
This closes the last bullet of s34.20 "still owed".

#### The self-review changed three things, all of them from measurement

The tidy reading of the two guard lines is WRONG and is not what shipped.
"267 covers form controls, 268 covers `<a>`/`<div>`/`<span>`" is false:
`.disabled` is a real boolean only on form controls and `undefined` on the
others, but an assignment there is an EXPANDO that reads `true`, so the
property guard fires on every tag. Measured across seven tags through the real
directive (`.probes/disabled-guards.test.ts`). The aria line is simply the only
signal the non-form tags have.

And WHERE line 267 does its work is not where it looks. Reconciled against the
parallel session's `.probes/disabled-click.test.ts`, which measured the channel
mine did not separate: a form control disabled BEFORE the click reaches no
listener at all, so the read never runs for it. It earns its place on the two
channels the platform leaves open - a tag the platform never suppresses, and a
control disabled DURING the dispatch, where the event is already in flight and
is NOT retracted (`["first","second"]`: a listener after the one that disabled
the element still runs). The second is exactly the rc.9 ordering, so 267 is the
line that reads a template handler's veto. Neither JSDoc would have said this
without that probe.

One row was CUT from the CHANGELOG table for being unmeasured: `aria-disabled`
was measured for the directive alone, never for a template `@click` setting it
mid-click, which is what that table is about.

#### Reconciliation with the parallel session

Its four probes were read and re-run here. Every shared figure agrees: the
`typeof` split per tag; directive-first `["cartAdd"]` against template-first
`[]`; `.delegate` unaffected in BOTH orders; direct `stopPropagation()`
surviving where `.delegate` does not. Two independent measurements of the same
table, which is the strongest thing this cycle has produced about any row.
Its `disabled-click` `dispatchEvent` arm stays TV per s34.20 (happy-dom only)
and nothing documented here rests on it.

#### PROCESS: the gate step-9 diagnosis on record was wrong

It was reported failing at step 9 "only because it ran docs before the build".
It is not that. `npm run docs` is idempotent here - two consecutive runs, byte
identical diff - and `scripts/gate.mjs` step 9 is
`git diff --exit-code -- docs/api` AGAINST HEAD, so it fires on any uncommitted
docs/api change whether stale or not. Step 11 wants a clean tree for the same
reason. The gate is built to run on a COMMITTED tree; commit first, gate after.
Running build before docs is still right, it is simply not what was failing.

#### Item 5, measured and PENDING OWNER: the plugin on a Vapor app

`createVaporApp(App).use(createDirectivePlugin())` registers the vDOM OBJECT
directive on a Vapor app. rc.9 warns and skips, so every `v-vc:command` is
inert; rc.8 threw a TypeError at mount. Our JSDoc says to use `vcCommandVapor`
there, in prose, with nothing enforcing it.

DETECTION IS AVAILABLE and needs no `vue` import: measured, a Vapor app carries
an own `vapor` key and a vDOM app does not (own-key diff `["vapor"]` against
`[]`), while `_context` has the identical key set on both. One property read.

brotli; the three IIFEs carry no directives code and are unaffected:

    B  throw our own message              +170 raw / +46 br

### 34.23 The two checks the cycle owed, run at last (s40)

Both were owed and neither had been run. The second is the more serious
omission: every directive test in this repo runs WITHOUT the interop plugin
this package re-exports, which was known and had been left standing.

#### The `<template v-for :key>` check: 01dba84c, 37b85739, 052c7688

s34.18 point 3 pulled these back to plain TV on the right argument - a grep for
`withVaporDirectives` cannot see how key and order codegen reach us. The path
is: keys decide whether an element carrying `v-vc:command` is REUSED or
RECREATED, that decides when the directive scope is disposed, and that decides
whether `unmountCommand` runs at all - with `.delegate`, whether the
per-document refcount is decremented.

So MOUNTS AND CLEANUPS ARE COUNTED, not inferred from whether a click works.
A click still working is exactly what a stranded listener looks like.
`.probes/vfor-keys-and-interop.test.ts`, compiled template, real mounts:

    <ul><template v-for="it in items" :key="it.id">
      <li><button v-vc:command="it.act">{{ it.id }}</button></li>
    </template></ul>

    step                              mounts  cleanups  note
    mount [a,b,c]                        3        0
    keyed reorder -> [c,b,a]             3        0      element REUSED, moved
                                                         to index 2; directive
                                                         did not re-run
    click new index 0                                    -> addC: the binding
                                                         travelled with its node
    filter out the middle                3        1      exactly one
    app.unmount()                        3        3      BALANCED

Identical in BOTH host shapes (plugin absent and installed). The `.delegate`
variant of the same list: 3 mounts / 3 cleanups, and document click listeners
added 1 / removed 1 - no stranded shared listener.

So the three rows are answered for this library: keyed reuse across a reorder
does not re-run the directive and does not leak, and a filtered row runs its
cleanup once. `01dba84c` and `37b85739` move to V; `052c7688` was already V
and its consumer effect is now measured rather than owed.

#### The interop host shape, which had never been exercised

`withVaporDirectives` has two host shapes and the suite only ever drove one.
Installing `vaporInteropPlugin` flips `isInteropEnabled`, which is what gives
the rc.9 root-chain visitor its `onInteropFragment` arm (e35e9af1). Re-run
under it:

    compiled click, plugin installed   -> ["cartAdd"]
    after app.unmount()                -> []          (listener gone)
    mounts / cleanups                  -> 1 / 1
    the whole v-for table above        -> identical to the plugin-free run

No difference found. That is the point of running it: the claim "our directive
behaves the same in a mixed tree" was previously untested in the only host
shape where it could have failed.

README subpath table (line 1286, `v-vc:command` only). Neither states anything
FALSE; neither lists the other two directives at all.

AND THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT EQUAL, which none of the three sentences says.
`v-vc:payload` has a documented substitute - `data-vc-payload`, and a consumer
can bind it. `v-vc:optimistic` has NO substitute: `state.optimisticFn` is set
only by the vDOM `vc-optimistic` registration, so optimistic updates with
rollback are UNAVAILABLE in a Vapor template. That is a capability gap, not a
documentation one, and it is bigger than most of what this cycle has turned up.
Flagged for the owner, not designed here.

#### MEASURED CONSEQUENCE the plan did not predict: the vue-tsc gap closes

s34.6 recorded that vue-tsc type-checks the template call by passing the ARGUMENT
as a raw string, so the imported-binding form fails `vue-tsc --noEmit` with
TS2345. With no argument there is nothing to mis-check.

**THE FIRST A/B THAT "PROVED" THIS WAS INVALID, and the reason is the finding.**
It used `import { vcCommandVapor as vVc }` on BOTH arms. Vue resolves an SFC
directive by camelCasing the FULL name: `v-vc:command` looks for `vVc` (the
directive is `vc`, `command` is its argument), but `v-vc-command` looks for
`vVcCommand`. So on the hyphen arm there was no declaration to resolve, and
vue-tsc passed for exactly the "nothing to check" reason the app-wide workaround
passed - the outcome the probe existed to distinguish. A TS2339 control proved
the template was checked for EXPRESSIONS, which is not the same as proving the
directive binding resolved. The conclusion happened to be right; the evidence did
not support it.

Re-run with each arm naming its own binding, and a fourth arm for the failure
mode that misled the first run:

    OLD colon  v-vc:command   binding vVc          exit 2   TS2345 on the argument
    NEW hyphen v-vc-command   binding vVcCommand   exit 0   clean
    CONTROL    hyphen + a deliberate type error    exit 2   TS2339 - and the message
                                                            ENUMERATES vVcCommand's
                                                            full signature, which is
                                                            what proves the binding
                                                            is in scope and resolved
    CONTROL    hyphen + the WRONG binding (vVc)    exit 0   passes silently, which is
                                                            why arm 2 alone proved
                                                            nothing

The third arm is the one the first attempt lacked. Corroborated independently and
more strongly by the example itself: `examples/vapor-sfc` now imports the binding,
uses it, passes its own `vue-tsc --noEmit` build step, and its control genuinely
dispatches under `npm run check:example`.

**The tool has NOT caught up** - the colon form still fails and any directive
taking an argument still trips it. What changed is that this package no longer
has the shape that triggers it.

#### THE BINDING NAME CHANGES, and it fails silently - caught by one gate

`v-vc-command` resolves to `vVcCommand`, not `vVc`. An import left aliased to
`vVc` COMPILES, TYPE-CHECKS AND MOUNTS NOTHING: the same silent dead control
#15490 produced, reintroduced by the fix for it.

It happened here. The example was switched to the imported form with the old
alias, `vue-tsc` passed, `vite build` passed, and
`scripts/check-example-directive.mjs` caught it - it clicks the built page's
button and asserts `vc-loading` and `disabled`. Nothing else in the repo would
have. That script was written after #15490 for precisely this failure mode, and
it has now paid for itself twice.

It is an upgrade note in the CHANGELOG, not a footnote.

#### The vue-tsc gap check: DELETED (owner, 2026-09-22)

`npm run check:tsc-gap` and `scripts/check-vue-tsc-directive-gap.mjs` are gone,
and `examples/vapor-sfc` is back on the imported form.

Settled by history rather than by argument. The option of "keep app-wide
registration, it is also a legitimate style" rests on a false premise: `f902a15`

Rejected, with reasons worth keeping:

- re-pointing the script at the colon form as an upstream tracker - it would

  reason that cannot affect us. That is an assertion that cannot fail, in mirror
  image, and its red is more convincing than a green-forever guard's silence;
- leaving it red - "that one's always 2" is how a gate stops being read.

On the script's own header, which says to delete it when it fails "because the
tool caught up": the reason did not happen but the instruction still holds. A
reopen condition that fires for an unanticipated cause is still doing its job -
it became inconclusive at precisely the moment it stopped being able to tell us
anything.

WHAT IS NOT DELETED WITH IT: the knowledge. The upstream bug still exists, and
the CHANGELOG now carries one sentence saying the gap is unreachable through
`v-vc-command` because there is no argument to mistype. That is evidence for the
architecture decision - the reshape removed a class of upstream exposure, not

### 34.27 Section 4a implemented: the two vDOM-only directives ported to Vapor (s43, 2026-09-22)

Owner decision: **B2**. Sized first with no code (three options), then built.

#### The sizing that decided it

    option                                   raw     brotli   vs keeping as-is
    C  keep as-is                          21,546    7,049    -
    A  drop the two vDOM-only              21,127    6,973    -419 /  -76
    B1 port, order-dependent               22,217    7,164    +671 / +115
    B2 port, order-independent             22,039    7,168    +493 / +119
    B2 AS SHIPPED                          22,046    7,174    +500 / +125

Vite production consumer bundle of `./directives`, brotli q11, entry
`import * as` so the new exports count - so the absolute numbers differ from
rc9/56's named-import figure and only the deltas compare. The prototype
predicted the shipped cost to within 7 raw / 6 brotli. `./directives` is not
budgeted; all three IIFEs are byte-identical, which is the control. The `.d.ts`
grows 3,238 B / 65 lines for two exports, and reaches no consumer's bundle.

**THE OWNER CORRECTED THE PLAN'S FRAMING, and the correction changed the
answer's shape.** `directive-reshape-plan.md` posed 4a as "one directive plus
attributes, or keep three" - two options, both of which remove or keep. The
asymmetry can be removed in EITHER direction, and levelling UP was never
offered. B is the option the plan did not contain.

#### What the measurement corrected in my own analysis

I expected `data-vc-payload` to be weak on REACTIVITY. It is not: a bound
`:data-vc-payload="JSON.stringify(...)"` tracks a changing payload on BOTH
renderers, because the attribute is read fresh at dispatch. Measured, not
assumed.

Where it is actually weak is FIDELITY, and that is what defeats option A:

    value in the payload    via the binding        via data-vc-payload
    Date                    Date instance          ISO string
    Map                     Map instance           {}
    class instance          instance               plain object
    function                function               DROPPED
    key set to undefined    key present            key GONE

And for optimistic there is no substitute at all. A Vapor consumer had to drop
`v-vc-command` for that button and hand-roll the dispatch, losing
`vc-loading` / `vc-error`, disable-while-busy, the re-entrancy guard, the
timeout and the modifiers - and could not recover them by adding an `@click`
beside the directive, because `80b3a046` makes that handler register FIRST and
`buildHandler`'s guards let it veto the dispatch. So A is not removing
redundancy; it is removing capability and asking consumers to rebuild the rest
by hand. Under the no-removal-for-zero-consumers rule it needed a positive case
and did not have one.

#### B2 over B1, staged rather than argued

A compiled Vapor template applies an element's directives in SOURCE order, and
`mountCommand()` opens by calling `unmountCommand()`, which DELETES the
element's state. So the naive port loses

    <button v-vc-payload="p" v-vc-command="a">

- the button dispatches with no payload, silently. B1 can only warn about it,
and attribute order is not something a consumer has reason to think matters.
B2 holds an unclaimed getter in a weak `pendingVapor` map that `mountCommand`
claims BEFORE building the state literal (so the two slots stay part of the one
hidden-class shape the literal's own note requires).

STEP 1 was to verify that before anything else was written, on compiled
templates in both orders. It passes both, and reducing the shipped code to B1's
shape fails exactly the payload-before-command case - from TWO independent
injections, dropping the slot and dropping the pickup. Four brotli bytes.

#### Arming

Five injections into `src/directives.ts`, each restored by in-memory copy in a
finally with the restore asserted identical. All five went red and named their
case: the B1 reduction, the pickup, the dispatch-time payload read, the
dispatch-time optimistic read, and reading the payload at mount instead of
dispatch.

Two cases in the new block are labelled in the file as NOT fails-before: the
SFC alias test pins upstream compiler behaviour, and the assignability test is
a type assertion that fails at `tsc`.

#### The rc9/57 alias rule, carried

The bindings are `vVcPayload` and `vVcOptimistic`. A shorter alias compiles,
type-checks, and falls back to `resolveDirective("vc-payload")`, which finds
nothing - Vue warns in DEV and the warning is STRIPPED from the production build
the example ships, which is exactly how the same mistake reached a built example
in rc9/57.

Three places now carry it: an upgrade note, the example, and two guards. The
example's optimistic function bumps by `cmd.payload?.qty ?? 1` and the binding
carries `qty: 3`, so one observable answers both directives AND discriminates -
`npm run check:example` reads 3 when the payload is live and 1 when it is dead.
Armed by renaming each alias in the example: the payload arm reports
`optimistic 0 -> 1, expected 3`, the optimistic arm reports `stayed at 0`.

#### A gate gap found on the way, and closed

`rc9/58` added `scripts/check-console-shape.mjs` to `lint:check` but not to
`scripts/gate.mjs`, whose lint step enumerates its pieces BY HAND. So a
console-shape violation would have passed every `npm run gate` run. Added, with
the reason written at the list, because the list invites exactly this.

### 35.3 Rows with contact, against our call paths

A fix commit says what upstream believed was broken. Each row below is answered
against what THIS library calls, and says how it was reached.

**`ef5ff106` - a throwing subscriber no longer starves the rest of the batch.**
`flush()` wraps each `effect.notify()` in a try, drains the queue, resets it,
then rethrows the FIRST error. Upstream's three tests: a later effect, a later
watcher, and an unrelated later write all see what they should. Reaches us:
every `signal()` write on Vue is a `shallowRef` write that ends in this
`flush()`. The write still throws, so code after it is skipped exactly as on
rc.9; what changes is that the other subscribers of `loading`, `lastError` or a
command state are told. TO VERIFY by reading `chamber.ts`: no write site
depends on the abort. `npm run ab:vue -- 3.6.0-rc.9` is REQUIRED this cycle,
not skippable on "the reactivity dist is byte-identical": it is not.

**`506b333c` - inputs are delivered, not re-resolved.** One input effect per
component evaluates the parent's getters once per parent update and delivers
values (`propsValues`, one standalone `Dep` per key, `trackDep` /
`triggerDep`) inside one `startBatch` / `endBatch`. Deleted with it:
`isolatePropSources`, `isolateSlotSources` and their `shallowReactive` copies
under KeepAlive; a KeepAlive cache hit now REBINDS the cached instance to the
new call site's getters. `VaporElement` hands host props over as
`{ $: [() => this._props] }`, with the comment "a function property is not a
prop getter". `@vue/reactivity` gains `@internal` exports: `Dep`, `trackDep`,
`triggerDep`, `activeSub`, `startBatch`, `endBatch`. Reaches us four ways:

- `router/vapor.ts`: the outlet passes no props. It reads `{ slots }` off the
  instance in `setup`, and `initSlots` replaces `instance.slots` BEFORE setup
  runs, so `slots.default` reads the final proxy. By reading; the six outlet
  fixtures decide.
- `defineWidget` / `defineVaporCustomElement`: a host page that sets a
  FUNCTION on a widget property. On rc.9 it was treated as a getter and
  called; on rc.10 it arrives as the function. No doc or test of ours states
  either behaviour (`iife-elements.ts` and `chamber-vapor.ts` read in full).
- KeepAlive: `keepalive-input-scope-fixture`, `usecommand-keepalive`,
  `register-ownership` and `vapor-keepalive-fixture` all mount a real
  `VaporKeepAlive`, whose input scope was just rebuilt.
- Sizes: every Vue-bundled row in `docs/BUNDLE-SIZES.md`, the outlet guard and
  the example bundles will move. Direction unknown until built.

**`437abc2a` `8cf0c49c` `8d272536` `19c79908` - interop owns directive hooks
and follows the Vapor child's root.** runtime-core stops invoking directive and
vnode hooks for a Vapor child; interop does, per root-chain component: `created`
/ `beforeMount` before the root is inserted, `beforeUnmount` while it is still
connected, a REMOUNT when a branch switch replaces the root, `beforeUpdate` /
`updated` (not a remount) when a KeepAlive branch is reactivated, and only once
a pending async setup has settled. Hooks are handed the element that was
mounted (`extend({}, vnode, { el })`), not the current one.

Reaches us: `createDirectivePlugin()` on a vDOM app with `vaporInteropPlugin`,
and `<VaporChild v-vc-command="...">` in a vDOM parent. Our `mounted` /
`updated` / `beforeUnmount` now run against the element the child really
renders. The removed rc.9 lines set `vnode.dirs = null` when the root did not
resolve and never mounted on a replacement root, so a Vapor child whose root is
a `v-if` / `v-else` kept its listener on the element that left. Upstream's
"unmount with the bindings it was mounted with" is the rule at the top of
`directives.ts` (teardown is keyed to what was mounted), implemented on their
side of the call. NO FIXTURE OF OURS DRIVES THIS SHAPE: s34.23 ran the VAPOR
directive under interop, never the vDOM plugin on a Vapor child.

**`86d44991` `51193cc7` `19a7a43e` - listeners.** `:onXxx` on a native element
binds a listener (it was a property write). A root's own listeners and the
fallthrough ones share one invoker per key, own first. On an element with
`v-model`, same-element listeners are emitted after it. Custom directives are
still emitted LAST: `genCustomDirectives` follows the model block in
`genBlockContent`. Reaches us: the ordering table at the end of
`directives.ts` holds for `@click`. Two additions, both by reading:
`:onClick="fn"` beside `v-vc-command` now registers before us and can veto
like `@click`; and the merged invoker wraps `stopImmediatePropagation` but
still calls the platform's, so that veto still reaches our direct listener.

**`364fc0f0` `e9eef846` `b5ce2cee` - a root's class and style have two
layers.** Own binding and fallthrough are tracked apart; a token leaves only
when the layer that wrote it drops it and neither the other layer nor the
template holds it. Reaches us: the "Still watching" limitation in whitepaper
9.2. Scope unchanged, by reading: `vc-loading` on a component root is in no
layer's previous value, so nothing removes it; on a non-root element
`setClass` still assigns `className` wholesale. `$root` is now a meta object
where it was `true`; nothing in `src` reads it.

**`d2311bb3` - upstream re-asserts after a bound update, for its own
directive.** `<select v-model>` now re-applies its selection from the OWNER's
updated hooks, pushed onto `instance.u`, because the owner can re-render the
options without touching the model. That is s34.11 option (c), which we
recorded as unavailable on Vapor for want of a hook. It is still unavailable:
`instance.u` is internal, and a lifecycle hook inside a userland Vapor
directive still warns (rc.9 `4cffa134`). No unlock. It does settle what the
fix looks like if a public hook appears.

**`0cdb312b` `87b4c7c0` `9dd8cdbb` `08cad764` `20f46c11` `489e8cd7` - dynamic
component.** Every new branch is gated on `isInteropEnabled && isVNode(...)` or
on a `key` argument. Our outlet hands `createDynamicComponent` a `__vapor`
component, a slot block or a literal null, and no key, so it takes the rc.9
path line for line. Group A file, direct contact, no change - the same verdict
and the same method as `0e4ff650` in s34.13.

**`8faa3006` `b6f25b06` `bba7ea6e` `d8364a56` `daca5169` - KeepAlive.** A
cached component is restored by its explicit key; a KeepAlive's child counts as
the single root, so fallthrough attrs and a directive on `<KeepAlive>`'s parent
reach through it; managed mounts skip the cache lookup; the rest of a
`v-else-if` chain is stopped rather than paused. Reaches us through
`tryKeepAliveHooks` and `useCommand`'s release-on-deactivate. TO VERIFY by the
four fixtures named above; `chamber.ts` not re-read.

**`7d94c491` - rows of a keyed insert are created in source order.** It was
tail first. Creation order is registration order, and `register()` is
last-wins with ownership, so N rows registering ONE action now leave the last
row as owner where rc.9 left the first. Not a documented pattern; one line in
the upgrade notes if a probe confirms it.

**`5592ea3e` `a4bb6fee` `7372680b` - Transition, in-out mode.** Each leave is
handed to its own entering branch, a pending leave survives a props update,
and settled branches are released. Below the bridge, which supplies hook
bodies only. TO VERIFY: `transitions.ts` was not re-read, and no fixture of
ours runs `mode="in-out"`.

**`3a952ef5` and the `hmr.ts` half of `87b4c7c0` - HMR.** Dirty components stay
marked until the post-flush; a render-less component escalates past a vDOM
parent. `tests/hmr-render-scope-fixture.test.ts` and
`tests/vapor/vapor-outlet-hmr.test.ts` drive the real runtime.

**Custom elements: `030f158d` `a429b2a6` `0f9d0758`.** A hydrated custom
element mounts once; its children hydrate; a native slot outlet carries the
owner's scope id. Inherited by `defineWidget` consumers that server-render.

**Compiler only (17 rows).** They reach us through compiled output: the three
examples, and every fixture that goes through `tests/compile-vapor.ts`. Worth
naming: `1fdd8098` (static text and attribute values are no longer escaped
twice), `e5e75e97` (`compileScript` emits `<style module>` bindings and changes
what a non-inline Vapor `setup` returns; `tests/async-vapor-setup-fixture`
calls `compileScript`), `074501e2` (two `v-if` branches sharing a key is a
compile ERROR now).

### 35.4 The standing question: what does rc.10 unlock, improve, or make cheaper

**Unlocks - something in `src` we could delete or simplify: NONE FOUND in the
77 rows read.** Three candidates were looked at. None is closed: each is OPEN
until it is measured or the owner rules on it.

WHAT "@internal" MEANS HERE, because the first draft of this list used the word
as if it were a verdict, and the owner pulled it up: JavaScript has no public or
private export. `@internal` is a JSDoc tag in Vue's TypeScript source, and
Vue's type build sets `stripInternal: true` (`tsconfig.build.json` and
`scripts/build-types.js`, read at the rc.10 tag). So a tagged name is a REAL
export of the built module, importable and callable, and is only removed from
the published `.d.ts`. Two facts follow and nothing else does: the type checker
does not know the name, and upstream makes no promise to keep it. That is a
cost to weigh against a measured gain, not a reason to skip the measurement.
Precedent in this repo: `setActiveSub` has the same standing (whitepaper rc.4
entry), and `untracked()` was built on the typed `pauseTracking` /
`resetTracking` instead.

- `startBatch` / `endBatch`, exported from `@vue/reactivity` since `506b333c`
  (`packages/reactivity/src/index.ts`), which `src/vue.ts` already imports
  from. Use: batch the several signals one dispatch writes (`loading`,
  `lastError`, state). Expected gain, by reasoning only: render effects already
  collapse through the scheduler, so a SYNCHRONOUS subscriber reading two of
  our signals would run once instead of twice. UNMEASURED. Owes an interleaved
  A/B on the real dispatch path before any verdict, and a fixture that fails if
  a later RC drops the export (the `vue-bundler-vapor-exports` pattern).
- A standalone `Dep` with `trackDep` / `triggerDep` as a lighter `signal()`.
  Same standing: real exports, no types, no promise. `shallowRef` is what the
  wiring hands over today. UNMEASURED.
- An owner-updated hook for the Vapor directive (the `d2311bb3` shape). This
  one is different in kind: `instance.u` is a field on an instance object, not
  an export, and a Vapor directive is not handed the instance. Not reachable
  without `getCurrentInstance()`-style access that Vapor withholds by design.

**Improves - behaviour a consumer gets from the bump, each owing a fixture or a
note before it is claimed:**

1. The vDOM directive plugin on a Vapor child follows the child's root. The
   largest item, and untested here. Owes a compiled mixed-tree fixture: vDOM
   parent, Vapor child with a `v-if` / `v-else` root, `v-vc-command` on the
   child, mounts and cleanups COUNTED across a root switch and a KeepAlive
   round trip.
2. A function-valued property on a widget is a value. Owes a probe on both
   RCs, then one sentence in `defineWidget`'s docblock if it holds.
3. A throwing subscriber no longer hides a dispatch's state from the others.
4. In-out transitions, hydrated custom elements, KeepAlive restore by key.
5. `56500421`: the hydration locator cache is released when the pass ends, so
   a hydrated page stops retaining detached subtrees.

**Cheaper - Vue's, inherited, and ours to MEASURE rather than quote:** inputs
evaluated once per parent update with per-key deps; no `shallowReactive`
copies under KeepAlive; a root template's class and style parsed on first use
(`b5ce2cee`). What we own is the measurement: the outlet guard's two limits,
the Vapor wiring rows in `docs/BUNDLE-SIZES.md`, the two Vapor example bundles
against rc.9 on clean trees, and `ab:vue`.

### 35.5 Owed, in the order the procedure gives

1. The six TV rows read; the two TV-N rows signed off or read.
2. `chamber.ts`, `transitions.ts`, `store.ts`, `ssr.ts`, `vite-hmr.ts` read in
   full, and each TO VERIFY above turned into V or withdrawn.
3. An install. Then step 2 of `rc-alignment.md`: `vue` and every direct
   `@vue/*` devDependency, the peer range, the example pins; all three examples
   rebuilt and `npm run check:example`.
4. Build, both suites, the gates, `ab:vue -- 3.6.0-rc.9`.
5. The fixture in 35.4 item 1 and the probe in item 2, each run on rc.9 first.
6. Step 8's four places, under a NEW unreleased CHANGELOG heading: v1.25.0 is
   dated.

A git repository is needed before any of 3 to 6 can be gated: `npm run gate`
ends on `git diff` and `git status`. Owner's call.

READING ONLY, again. Owner: a local repository; made, `main` = the baseline

statement about what an upstream commit does is still unchecked here: the

### 35.11 F1 and F4 taken (fifth step, branch `outlet-slot-fix` off `rc10`)

Owner: fix our bugs and the doc gaps first, the rest is for discussion. So F1
and F4 of 35.10 are done here, on their own branch, and F2 (Vue's), F3, F5, F6,
F7 and F9 stand as written.

**F1, FIXED. The cause, V by reading Vue's source and by the test.** In the
installed runtime, `removeFragment(block)` ends with
`if (block.scope) block.scope.stop()`, and `DynamicFragment.update` calls it on
the previous branch. `createSlot('default')` with no fallback argument returns
a `DynamicFragment` whose scope holds the slot content's effects. The outlet
built that fragment once in setup and returned the same block from the
`createDynamicComponent` getter, so after a child route had replaced it the
block was re-inserted with its scope stopped.

    fails-before   tests/vapor/vapor-outlet.test.ts, new arm (g): a slot holding
                   a render effect, through a child route and back. Both arms
                   failed, the dev build and the executed production build:
                   "expected 'on' to be 'off'".
    the fix        with a default slot, the outlet returns
                     createIf(entryAt, matched, () => createSlot('default'), 261)
                   so the slot is created in the branch's scope each time the
                   branch is entered. That is, flags included, what
                   compiler-vapor emits for
                     <component :is="c" v-if="c" /><slot v-else />
                   and tests/vapor/vapor-outlet-helpers.test.ts recompiles that
                   template on the installed Vue and compares the flags with
                   the constant in `src/router/vapor.ts`. With NO default slot
                   there is no `createIf`: the empty branch must stay one node,
                   and arm (b) still pins it.
    after          3 passed; arms (a) to (f) unchanged. The compiled
                   conditional-slot probe of 35.8 item 8 now reads right in all
                   three arms, steps 6 to 8.
    rejected       creating the slot inside the `createDynamicComponent` getter:
                   the getter runs in the outlet's render effect, not in a
                   branch scope, so each navigation would allocate a fragment
                   nothing disposes (the reason the old comment gave, and it
                   holds). Calling `slots.default()` directly from a wrapper
                   component: it skips the slot fragment, its scope ids and its
                   boundary, and adds a component instance per fallback.

**F1, the cost. V (measured).**

    module alone, esbuild minified      831 -> 880 B min, 441 -> 471 B brotli
    its BUNDLE-SIZES row                unchanged: 0.8 / 0.5 / 0.4 KB
    outlet own arm, KB brotli           4.58 -> 4.74 (ceiling 5.0)
